transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-09-08
Time: 14:00 - 14:52 EST
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Carlos Ruiz (Redwood SE), Ellen Moore (Westmount Head of Cloud & Security), Daniel Kim (VP Platform), Priya Shah (Compliance)

Summary: quick discovery focused on data residency, logging and audit requirements for financial workloads; Westmount evaluating Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private, leaning toward Dedicated/Private due to logging retention and encryption keys. Next steps agreed: send compliance pack, schedule SE deep dive and plan pilot/benchmarks.

Topics: data residency (EU/US), GDPR scope, HIPAA considerations for consumer-facing lending product, KMS/HSM options, audit-log retention restrictions, network isolation (VPC), RBAC/SSO, SOC 2 evidence, on-prem sizing for private deployment.

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya: All right hi everyone thanks for making the time. This is Maya from Redwood, I'm the account lead for the account — with me is Carlos our solutions engineer.
[00:12] Ellen: Hi Maya hi Carlos thanks, we'll just do a quick round robin — I'm Ellen, Head of Cloud & Security at Westmount, this is Daniel Kim, VP platform, and Priya Shah who handles compliance.
[00:22] Maya: Great, can you share a bit of context — where you are in the evaluation and the primary drivers? Like is it latency, cost, or data residency and compliance?
[00:32] Daniel: Primarily compliance and residency. We've got a new consumer lending product, some of the user data is EU resident, we're regulated as a financial insitution so logs and auditability are big concerns. Latency is secondary.
[00:44] Priya: To add, we have strict rules about what logs leave our environment. We need full control of audit logs, retention policies, and ability to redact PII before anything goes out. Also, key management — customer-owned keys are preferable.
[00:57] Carlos: Totally, thank you. Quick high level: Redwood provides Hosted API, Dedicated reserved capacity, and Private (VPC/on-prem). Hosted is fastest but logs and keys are handled in Redwood infra; Dedicated gives reserved GPU pools with stronger isolation and can be region-pinned; Private can be customer-hosted with full control over keys and logs.
[01:18] Ellen: So for Hosted, how does data residency work? If a EU user makes a request, can we ensure the call stays in EU and logs never cross borders?
[01:27] Carlos: For Hosted we have regional endpoints, but some logs and control plane metadata may be replicated to the control plane in the US for operational reasons — that is call out in our docs. For strict residency and customer-managed KMS, Dedicated can be region-pinned and Private gives you full control.
[01:42] Priya: That replication is a no-go for us if it contains PII or transaction metadata. We need assurance that any raw logs with PII are either not collected or are stored in-region and under our KMS.
[01:53] Maya: Understood. We do offer options: redaction at the SDK/agent level, prefix / prompt-level caching control, and a privacy mode where we avoid storing request payloads — but some telemetry for infra health still exists. Carlos can walk through the log categories.
[02:08] Carlos: Yeah, we categorize telemetry: control-plane metadata (request id, model used, time), infra telemetry (latency, GPU metrics), and request/response payloads. For Private, you can disable payload capture entirely and keep all logs in your VPC. For Dedicated we can offer a narrower retention window and region restriction but not full on-prem control unless Private.
[02:28] Daniel: What about encryption? We need to use our own keys (KMS/HSM) and we require hardware-backed keys for certain workloads.
[02:36] Carlos: Private supports customer KMS and HSM integrations—bring-your-own-key via KMIP or cloud KMS. Dedicated can integrate with customer KMS in some configurations but usually via a secure link; Hosted uses Redwood-managed KMS unless you opt for enterprise package with dedicated KMS proxies.
[02:50] Ellen: Do you have SOC 2 and ISO evidence, and are you able to provide GDPR articles mapping and data processing agreements?
[02:57] Maya: Yes, we are SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001 in progress, and we provide a DPA and GDPR mapping doc for customers — I'll send those after the call.
[03:07] Priya: And HIPAA? We might have some parts of the product touching health info for certain loan underwriting sources.
[03:12] Maya: HIPAA support is available but depends on deployment model; Private and Dedicated are the recommended routes. We can sign a BAA for Private deployments; Hosted is more complicated and would require strict contract addenda.
[03:26] Ellen: Can you clarify what you retain in Hosted vs Dedicated? For example, do you keep full request/response transcripts for 30 days by default?
[03:34] Carlos: Default Hosted retention is 30 days for request/response payloads, but in Hosted we also keep some aggregated logs longer for billing and analytics. Dedicated defaults to 14 days for payloads and longer infra logs — but retention is configurable. In Private you control retention policies entirely.
[03:51] Daniel: We need immutable audit logs for 7 years for certain transactions and the ability to produce these for audits. Can Redwood support that?
[03:59] Carlos: Yes — Private can store immutable logs in your archive (object store) under your retention policy. For Dedicated we can ship logs into your long-term archive via secure transfer, but you'd want Private if you need on-box immutability + HSM-backed signing.
[04:14] Priya: Does Redwood do any PII redaction automatically? Or is that on us to do pre-send?
[04:20] Maya: We have client SDK hooks for automatic PII masking and we can recommend a pre-processing layer. We also have prompt-level redaction tools in the console for evaluations. But for full compliance we recommend redaction before requests leave your network in Private or a pre-filter proxy in front of Dedicated/Hosted.
[04:39] Ellen: About logging restrictions — auditors often require that request bodies never be accessible by third parties. If your engineering team needs to debug, how does that work?
[04:49] Carlos: We have an escape hatch: for Private, everything stays in your environment and Redwood support can be given access under a jumpbox with customer approval. For Dedicated we can provide sanitized artifacts. Hosted support access is strictly controlled and covered by our SOC and internal policies but not ideal for sensitive financial PII.
[05:05] Daniel: Any certifications around network isolation? We use VPC peering and private endpoints — we need to avoid public internet paths.
[05:12] Carlos: Private uses your VPC; Dedicated supports VPC peering and private connectivity (e.g., PrivateLink equivalents). Hosted has regional private endpoints for enterprise customers in select clouds.
[05:23] Priya: One other ask — we need log hashing or signing so logs can't be tampered with. Is that supported?
[05:30] Carlos: For Private, yes — you can run an HSM to sign log batches. For Dedicated we can work with partners to implement signing. Hosted doesn't provide built-in customer-ownership signing today.
[05:41] Maya: sounds like Dedicated may be the sweet spot but Private is safer for the long run if you want full control. What's your timeline for pilot?
[05:48] Ellen: We're aiming to have a pilot by Q4, decision by end of year. We have procurement cycles and internal security review.
[05:55] Maya: Great that's doable. On pricing — Dedicated has a monthly reserved commit model; Private is project/engagement priced due to onsite work. I'll send ballpark numbers in the follow-up.
[06:06] Daniel: For the pilot we'll probably want a small Dedicated cluster in EU region and a POC to validate latency and that logs are handled as we expect.
[06:14] Carlos: For benchmarks we'll capture p99 latency, token throughput and also show KV cache behavior. Note I might call it K V cache in the notes cause transcription is weird.
[06:26] Priya: A compliance question — if a user requests data deletion under GDPR, can you purge from all backups and logs?
[06:33] Carlos: We can configure deletion paths: in Private you fully control deletion. In Dedicated we can implement fast-delete for payloads and mark backups for deletion per policy, but there is sometimes a residual in infra analytics for a short window; that's typically within your retention window config.
[06:50] Ellen: Auditors ask for access control proof—SSO, SAML, RBAC. What's supported?
[06:56] Maya: We support SAML SSO, SCIM provisioning, and fine-grained RBAC in the console for Hosted and Dedicated. In Private you can integrate with your internal identity systems.
[07:07] Daniel: Are there restrictions on redaction automation? Like can we blacklist partial account numbers and have them never be logged?
[07:14] Carlos: Yes, you can configure redaction rules in the SDK and on the pre-filter. We recommend client-side scrubbing for anything that must not leave your environment.
[07:23] Priya: Liability and contract: we need to see sample DPAs and also ensure contractually that Redwood won't use data for model training.
[07:30] Maya: We do not use customer payloads to train models unless explicitly opted-in. We'll include that language in the DPA and your contract.
[07:38] Ellen: Great. Could you also show where logs are stored in Dedicated — is it in Redwood-managed S3 or can we push to our own storage?
[07:46] Carlos: Typically Dedicated uses a customer-dedicated bucket in the same region; you can decide if it's a Redwood-managed bucket or one you control via cross-account role.
[07:58] Daniel: We also need to capture cost controls — token-level cost breakdowns per route and ability to throttle. Is that exposed?
[08:05] Maya: Yes console shows token-level cost breakdown, per-route dashboards, and rate-limiting controls. Those are part of Redwood Console.
[08:13] Priya: A technical detail — do you support hardware GPU isolation or any tenancy controls for Dedicated?
[08:19] Carlos: Dedicated offers tenant isolation at cluster level; hardware multi-tenancy is avoided for Dedicated since it's reserved pools. Private gives full hardware control.
[08:28] Ellen: Any examples of other banks using Private?
[08:31] Maya: We have references — I can connect you with one of our customers under an NDA for a quick reference call.
[08:38] Daniel: Ok that's helpful. On HIPAA: what's the process for BAA?
[08:42] Maya: For Private we can sign a BAA. For Dedicated we can discuss limited BAA language but it depends on the control plane footprint. We'll include legal contacts in the follow-up.
[08:52] Priya: Regarding retention windows — we may need per-client retention policies. Can Redwood support per-tenant retention?
[08:58] Carlos: Yes, both Dedicated and Private can enforce per-tenant retention and per-route policies, Hosted less so.
[09:06] Ellen: We also have a question about data residency in backups and DR. If we replicate across regions for DR, can that be disabled?
[09:12] Carlos: For Private you control DR replication. For Dedicated you can restrict replication; some infra metadata might be replicated for failover but payloads can be controlled. We'll need to confirm specifics for the EU legal requirements.
[09:26] Maya: I'll follow up with a short doc that maps Hosted/Dedicated/Private behavior for backups/DR.
[09:33] Priya: Ok thanks. Can we talk about logging format — we need structured, searchable logs with specific fields to feed into Splunk/ELK.
[09:41] Carlos: We export logs in JSON LTS format with field mappings; you can push to your SIEM via secure forwarder or we can push to your cloud bucket.
[09:50] Daniel: For the pilot we'll want to set up a small Dedicated cluster in eu-west-1, send sample traffic and check logs, KMS, latency. Can you provide infra checklist?
[09:59] Carlos: Yes I'll send a pilot infra checklist — it includes VPC peering steps, firewall rules, role mappings, and required object storage.
[10:07] Ellen: Any gotchas about egress? We need to ensure no unintended egress to third-party analytics providers.
[10:13] Maya: We don't forward payloads to third-party telemetry, but some hosted analytics might aggregate anonymized metrics; we'll make sure to disable any cross-account integrations for the pilot.
[10:24] Priya: One more: logging retention for billing purposes — if we turn off payload logging, will we still get accurate billing?
[10:31] Carlos: We can provide aggregated billing metrics without raw payloads; token counts are tracked at route level.
[10:37] Daniel: Great. Anything else on compliance?
[10:40] Priya: I'd like to see an example DPA and the GDPR Article mapping.
[10:44] Maya: We'll include those.
[10:46] Maya: quick recap of next steps — I'll send SOC 2, GDPR mapping, HIPAA / BAA note, and ballpark pricing. Carlos will send pilot checklist and benchmark plan. Ellen will share retention and classification policy.
[10:58] Ellen: Sounds good.
[11:00] Daniel: One more operational question — how do you handle model rollouts and regressions? We need a way to rollback quickly if a model causes bad outputs.
[11:08] Carlos: We support canary rollouts, A/B testing, automatic fallback to earlier model variants and per-route pinned versions. You can also disable certain routes via the console.
[11:20] Priya: Do you keep model input/output hashes for traceability?
[11:24] Carlos: We can store hashes — in Private you can configure full traceability with signed logs. In Dedicated we can also provide traces but hashed to protect payloads.
[11:37] Maya: Ok, question for Westmount — would you prefer we start with a Dedicated EU cluster pilot or go straight to Private?
[11:45] Ellen: Start Dedicated pilot to validate pipeline, then plan Private for production if that meets compliance gaps. Procurement wise Dedicated is faster.
[11:53] Maya: Perfect. We'll get timelines aligned.
[11:57] Carlos: I'll also outline required HSM/KMS options in the pilot doc.
[12:02] Priya: Thanks.
[12:04] Maya: Any final questions?
[12:06] Ellen: Not from me.
[12:07] Daniel: No.
[12:08] Priya: Nothing else.
[12:09] Maya: Great thanks everyone. We'll follow up with docs and set up the SE deep dive for next week.
